label: Cursor CLI
description: One conversation with Cursor CLI, Cursor's coding agent: three conversations are three nodes. Wire `agent` and `stream` into an AskAgent and talk to it in a Loop; end the loop with a CloseBus on `stream`, which ends this node's part of the run. With no `computer`, Cursor CLI runs on your machine (a local install only) from your own install of `agent` with your own login, working in `folder`. If `agent` is missing, weft installs it into a folder of its own, shared by the whole machine, before the node runs. With a `computer` wired, it is installed and run inside that computer, which a cloud install needs, and it logs in with the connection on `access`. The folder is always trusted (`--trust`), since Cursor's own prompt for it could not be answered. Its questions offer options only, with no answer of your own, and a plan it proposes comes out as a permission to accept or reject. Its card shows what it is doing and a Start over button. What is exposed: the permission mode, the model, Cursor's sandbox and extra folders. Your program's tools reach Cursor's model as the tools of an MCP server named `weft` (Cursor shows a call as `weft: <tool>`), and come back to your program under their plain names. When Cursor refuses a turn for something its account must do (sign in, upgrade its plan, add a payment method), it says so as a message rather than an error; weft fails that turn with Cursor's words. Cursor CLI cannot let a program's tool take one of its own tools' places, so a tool named like one of them (`Read`, `Shell`, `WebSearch` and the rest of this node's list) is refused when the program is built.

inputs.name: computer
inputs.description: A Computer to run Cursor CLI in. Left out, it runs on your machine, which only a local install has. Several agents may share one computer.

inputs.name: access
inputs.description: A CursorCliAccess's `access`: a Cursor API key. Required with a `computer`. Left out on your machine, Cursor CLI uses the login already on it.

inputs.name: folder
inputs.label: Folder
inputs.description: The folder Cursor CLI works in. On your machine it is required, and must exist. In a computer it is a path inside the computer, its home folder when left out.

inputs.name: program
inputs.label: Program
inputs.description: On your machine: the Cursor CLI program to run, when it is not the `agent` on your PATH or the one weft installs (an install of your own, a version you keep for this). A path on your machine, so it cannot go with a `computer`.

inputs.name: permission
inputs.label: Permissions
inputs.description: What Cursor CLI may do without asking. `ask`: every request it would put to a person comes out of AskAgent as a question. `plan`: it only plans, and proposes the plan for you to accept. `bypass`: every command its allowlist does not deny runs without asking (`--force`); a team whose admin forbids that falls back to asking.

inputs.name: model
inputs.label: Model
inputs.description: A model id Cursor offers your account, such as `gpt-5` or `sonnet-4-thinking` (`agent models` lists them). Left out, Cursor's default.

inputs.name: streamBy
inputs.label: Stream by
inputs.description: What goes out on `stream`: `message`, one event per whole message, tool use and result, so a run waiting on a long step sleeps; `token`, every piece of text as it is written too, which keeps the run awake while the agent writes.

inputs.name: sandbox
inputs.label: Sandbox
inputs.description: Whether its commands run in Cursor's sandbox, which needs unprivileged user namespaces on Linux. Left out, Cursor's own setting.

inputs.name: addDirs
inputs.label: Extra folders
inputs.description: Folders besides `folder` Cursor CLI may read and change.

outputs.name: agent
outputs.description: The agent's handle: wire it into AskAgent's `agent`. Baked: made when the infra is started.

outputs.name: stream
outputs.description: Everything the agent does in this run, as AskAgent sends it. Wire it into every AskAgent of the loop, and into a CloseBus after the loop: the run's part of this node ends when it does.

then.message: CursorCli '{id}' runs on the machine weft runs on, which a cloud install does not have; wire a Computer into `computer`.
CursorCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where no login is waiting for it; give it a CursorCliAccess on `access`.
CursorCli '{id}' works on your machine, so it needs a `folder` to work in.
CursorCli '{id}' has a `permission` it does not know; pick one of ask, plan, bypass.
CursorCli '{id}' has a `streamBy` it does not know; pick message or token.
CursorCli '{id}' runs in a computer, where `program`, a path on your machine, means nothing; leave `program` out, the computer installs Cursor CLI itself.
